Name: tropical_etm_deconvolution_hbm
Title: Deconvolving Drivers of Tropical Ocean Deoxygenation Across the Eocene Thermal Maximum: A Hierarchical Bayesian Assimilation of Multi-Proxy Data into an Earth System Model
Experiment: We will target existing and newly acquired sediment cores from tropical Pacific ODP/DSDP sites (e.g., Sites 1218, 865) spanning the ETM interval. Datasets include high-resolution I/Ca in benthic foraminifera (Cibicidoides spp.), redox-sensitive metal isotopes (e.g., δ238U, δ98Mo), lipid biomarker preservation indices (e.g., lycopane/n-alkane ratios), and boron isotope-based pH reconstructions (δ11B) to constrain carbonate chemistry. A transient ensemble of cGENIE Earth system model simulations will be performed, varying climate sensitivity, ocean ventilation rates, and organic carbon export within published uncertainty ranges. The primary metric is the reduction in posterior oxygen estimate uncertainty (95% credible intervals) compared to a proxy-only approach; secondary metrics include spatial pattern skill assessed by leave-one-out cross-validation at sites with independent records. Baseline comparisons will contrast the full hierarchical assimilation against: (i) uncalibrated proxy stacking, (ii) assimilation into a static box model, and (iii) a forward-only model without data constraints. Expected outcomes are probabilistic maps of oxygen concentrations at 10 kyr resolution, revealing that temperature-driven solubility loss dominated tropical deoxygenation, with productivity increases contributing mainly in equatorial upwelling zones. Ablation studies will systematically remove individual proxy types, the age-model integration, or the mechanistic model component (using a simple statistical interpolator) to quantify each element's contribution to uncertainty reduction and mechanistic attribution.
